For error to occur, [latex]Y_{K} \lt 10^{-6} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2 \times 10^{-6}&+N_{K}\lt 10^{-6} \\ N_{K} & \lt -10^{-6} \\ P(0 / 1) &=\int_{-\infty}^{-10^{-6}} P_{N K}(n) d n \\ &=\int_{-\infty}^{-10^{-6}} 0.5 \alpha e^{\alpha n} d n \text { with } \alpha=10^{7} \\ P(0 / 1) &=0.5 e^{-10} \end{aligned}[/latex]
When a '0' is transmitted:
[latex] Y_{K}=N_{K} [/latex]
For error to occur, [latex]Y_{K} \gt 10^{-6} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \; P(1 / 0)=\int_{10^{-6}}^{\infty} P_{N K}(n) d n=0.5 \times e^{-10} [/latex]
since, both bits are equiprobable;
[latex] P(0)=P(1)=\frac{1}{2} [/latex]
the probability of bit error
[latex] =P(1) \cdot P(0 / 1)+P(0) \cdot P(1 / 0) [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{P(0 / 1)+P(1 / 0)}{2}=0.5 \times e^{-10}[/latex]
